issue.title: test_format_agent_option_active_family_uses_nested_monitor_runtime expects 2m/2m but nested monitor starters now make the family total 3m
issue.description:
`test_format_agent_option_active_family_uses_nested_monitor_runtime` asserts the root
row's family runtime suffix renders `🏃‍♂️ 2m / 2m`, but it now renders `🏃‍♂️ 2m / 3m`.

Root cause: commit `2c8422053` ("fix(ace): count monitor starters in family runtime")
changed the family-total runtime computation in `src/sase/ace/tui/models/agent_time.py`
so a running nested monitor's own elapsed time counts toward the family total. In that
fixture the monitor starts at 09:03 and `now` is 09:05, so the family total is now 3m,
not 2m.

That commit updated its sibling assertions in
`tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_agent_list_runtime_compute.py` but missed
`tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_agent_list_runtime_rendering.py`, which had been split out of
the same original file by `f2f0bd977` ("test: split agent-list runtime rendering tests
under 500-line files"). The rendering test's expectation was left at the pre-change value.

Fix: decide whether `2m / 3m` is the intended family total for a running nested monitor
(it matches the intent of `2c8422053`) and update the assertion in
`tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_agent_list_runtime_rendering.py:254` — or, if the rendering
path should not count the monitor, fix `agent_time.py` instead.

Discovered while landing epic `sase-w8.4`; proposed by phase bead `sase-w8.4.1` note #2.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: Deterministic: the fixture pins start/run_start/stop and an explicit now=2026-07-19 09:05, so there is no clock or ordering nondeterminism. Reproduced on a clean master tree at c0b741c93 with a freshly reinstalled venv, serially with -p no:randomly, and independently reported by phase agent sase-w8.4.1 in a separate full-suite run. The 1m delta is exactly the running nested monitor's elapsed time that 2c8422053 started counting.
